# AGENTS.md · building AI Widgets for Landbot (for coding agents)

You are building interactive widgets that appear inside a Landbot AI agent's messages in the v4 web chat. Read this file first.

## The model in one paragraph
The AI agent ends its message with a tag, `[[prefix:name key=value lang=xx]]`. The bot's Custom JS (`runtime/lbw.js` + your widgets) finds the tag in the chat's DOM, removes it, validates every value against closed lists, and draws a widget from **your** data (code, a public API, or Landbot fields). Widget buttons can post a message **as the visitor** (the agent answers it) and write **Landbot fields** with that message. Flow messages can carry tags too, with `@{field}` values that Landbot fills in.

## The short path: the library and a JSON config
The runtime, the kit and their CSS are one versioned library, `lbw-kit`, loaded by URL. A bot's widgets are one JSON object, `LBW.kit.setup({…})`, with the kit's 20 types. **Start from an example**: copy `kit/example/config.json` or `kit/example-lead/config.json`, change the data, and run `npm run check:config -- config.json` until it prints no problem. Then `npm run bot -- config.json --out build` writes the bot's Custom JS and CSS from it. Write JavaScript only for what the JSON can't say.

Since v0.10 (the WOW layer) widgets move behind one gate (a visible tab, no reduced motion, `"motion": false` turns it off), live data says "● En directo" and highlights what changed, form/calc/review/slots are compact by default (`"density": "comfy"` for the old layout), and `calendar`, `map` and `tracker` are types.

## Non-negotiable rules
1. **The agent chooses, the code tells.** Never put prices, dates, specs or ranges in the agent's instructions. The tag carries ids, inputs, and values copied from a source (an action's answer, a field), never invented facts; the widget looks the rest up and checks every value (`params`). An invented id draws nothing.
2. **Every tag value is untrusted.** Use `p.one / p.list / p.num / p.text / p.day`. Set text with `textContent`, build URLs in code, and allow only your origins (`LBW.init({ links: ['https://shop.example/'] })`, each ending in `/`). Never use `innerHTML` with tag, API or field data.
3. **Tag characters must survive Markdown:** the chat renders Markdown before your code runs. Use `: , | =`, never `~ * _`.
4. **Copy, don't convert:** ask the model to copy values as written (a date, a slug) and convert in code. Validate, and show nothing rather than a guess.
5. **Quick replies send a sentence** in the visitor's language, through `LBW.ui.reply` / `LBW.say`. They're queued until the chat is quiet; a click mid-reply otherwise lands above the reply.
6. **Fields are written with a message:** `LBW.say(text, { field: value })`. They travel as `custom_data` in that message through the v4 widget (`LBW.landbot(this)`, written by `npm run bot`). `setCustomData` alone only queues them, a Code block's too.
7. **Unset fields aren't empty:** they arrive as `@{x}`, or as `Visitor #n` for `name`. `p.has()` handles it; always render a fallback.
8. **Widgets size to the chat, not the screen.** The column is 340 px on a phone, 672 px on tablet/desktop, ~350 px in a Livechat window. `lbw.css` fills it; lay out with `@container lbw (min-width: …)`, never `@media`.
9. **If a widget can show it, don't leave the agent.** Coming back from the flow failed twice: a re-entered agent block went dead, and a fresh agent answered the last message again (two cards). Use exits only for what the flow must do (validated questions, conditions, integrations, handover), and don't come back.
10. **Dates are computed in code, as UTC day numbers** (`p.day`, `LBW.day`), with "today" where the client is (`LBW.day.today('Europe/Madrid')`). The model never adds days.
11. **Instructions are code: test one case per rule.** Rule order matters: language first, then routing rules that override a widget's trigger ("BEFORE ANY OTHER RULE"), with the trigger words in every language. Refusals: "one sentence and NO tag at all".
12. **Publishing needs the bot owner's explicit yes, every time.** Use fake test data. Don't submit forms or accept consent banners on the client's live site.

## The runtime in 20 lines
```js
LBW.init({ prefix: 'np', langs: ['en','es'], defaultLang: 'en', links: ['https://shop.example/'], labels: { en: {…}, es: {…} } });
LBW.widget('card', function (p, ctx) {               // p = untrusted params, ctx = { lang, L, tag, message, prev }
  var id = p.one('id', IDS); if (!id) return null;    // null = draw nothing (the tag is still removed and logged)
  var o = LBW.ui.card(ctx.lang, 'np-card');           // .lbw > .lbw-box (o.box)
  LBW.ui.head(o.box, 'Kicker', DATA[id].name);
  LBW.ui.rows(o.box, [[ctx.L.price, DATA[id].price]]);
  LBW.ui.row(o, [LBW.ui.reply(ctx.L.details, ctx.L.more + DATA[id].name, { primary: true }),   // talks back
                 LBW.ui.link(ctx.L.buy + ' ↗', 'https://shop.example/' + DATA[id].url)]);     // leaves
  return o;
});
LBW.widget('size', function (p, ctx) {                // writes a field
  var g = LBW.ui.once('lbw-chips');                   // one-shot group
  ['s','m','l'].forEach(function (s) { g.appendChild(LBW.ui.reply(s.toUpperCase(), ctx.L.sizeSay + s.toUpperCase(), { fields: { size: s } })); });
  var o = LBW.ui.card(ctx.lang); o.box.appendChild(g); return o;
});
LBW.widget('summary', function (p, ctx) {             // reads fields a flow put in the tag: [[np:summary name=@{name}|size=@{size}|lang=@{lang}]]
  var o = LBW.ui.card(ctx.lang); LBW.ui.head(o.box, '', p.text('name', 40) || ctx.L.guest); return o;
});
```
Live data: `var o = LBW.ui.loading(ctx.lang, 'lbw-split'); return LBW.later(o, LBW.csv(URL), function (rows) { …fill o.box, return false if the id is unknown… }, fallback);`. Prefetch `LBW.csv(URL)` at load.
Hand-written widgets: `LBW.landbot(this);` once at the top level of your inline script, so sends go through the v4 widget (in a `<script src>` or a callback `this` isn't the widget; inline `var` isn't global, write `window.X`). Rows from a flow Code block: `LBW.data.get(key)` / `LBW.data.wait(key, ms)`.
A form that sends once: keep state, enable the CTA when required answers are in, `LBW.say(sentence, fields)` + `LBW.ui.done(group)`. Copy: clipboard → `execCommand` → a selected box.
Call button: `LBW.ui.tel(ctx.L.call, row.phone, '', '33')` with `'tel:'` in `links`. Photos: `LBW.ui.img(url, 'lbw-media', { srcset: [[u360, 360], [u640, 640]], width: 640, height: 400 })`.
Multi-select: `LBW.ui.multi([[key, label], …], 'Continue', function (keys) { return [text, { field: keys.join(',') }]; })`.
Free-text fields in a flow tag: put them **first**, separate every key with `|` (a visitor's `|` can add keys, and `]]` can close the tag).
Debug globals: `__lbwDropped` (what was thrown away, with the reason), `__lbwSent` (after the quiet wait), `__lbwStored`. On the widget: `data-tag`, `data-widget`.

## Where things break
| # | Break | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | The model wrote a value differently (`a b`, `a+b`, `Symi-Fast`, a translated slug) | Tolerant parsing + normalisation + repair against your data or API |
| 2 | Markdown ate a separator | Markdown-neutral characters; read `data-tag` in tests |
| 3 | The text contradicts the widget | Keep data out of the prompt; "the widget shows the data, not you" |
| 4 | A reply in the wrong language (a name alone, an unsupported language) | A `lang` field each turn; one-word messages keep the previous language; others → English |
| 5 | A quick reply landed above the reply it answered | Queue until quiet (built into `LBW.say`) |
| 6 | Chips repeat the question just asked | Filter on `ctx.prev` in code |
| 7 | "Visitor #537058751" as a name | Don't interpolate `@{name}` on paths that didn't ask it; `p.has()` |
| 8 | A field "not saved" | Fields go with a message |
| 9 | Slow client API, ~10 s action limit | Test at concurrency 3; cache; warn |
| 10 | The agent went silent after a flow message, or a widget came twice | Don't leave the agent for what a widget can show |
| 11 | Fixed-width cards on a wide column, or the desktop layout in a Livechat | `lbw.css` + container queries |
| 12 | "Today?" got the wrong widget; a refusal still drew widgets | Routing rules first; "NO tag at all" |
| 13 | Battery "failures" that were the harness | Read every failure; compare the bubble with `data-say`; use `data-widget` |

## Files
- `runtime/lbw.js`, `runtime/lbw.css`: the runtime and base look. `runtime/fallback.js`: removes raw tags if the library fails to load.
- `kit/kit.js`, `kit/kit.css`: the widget makers. `kit/setup.js`: `LBW.kit.setup(config)`, the widgets from JSON, with `params` and `source: { data }`. `kit/example/config.json`, `kit/example-lead/config.json`: the two examples.
- `dist/`: the built library and `manifest.json` (sizes, hashes, `integrity`). `scripts/`: `build.mjs`, `check-config.mjs`, `bot-code.mjs` (`npm run bot`), `version.mjs`. `test/`: `npm test`.
